findings.text: Machine-check Intel bringup and corrected-error interrupt helpers are present but have no observable effect in this configuration, covering feature init and clear plus queue clear, re-enable, rediscover and recheck operations.
Bank presence is represented as a bitmap type sized by the configured maximum bank count.
Machine-check polling control uses three single-bit flags at successive low bit positions for timestamp logging, uncorrected-error logging, and queue-only handling without immediate logging.
APEI threshold persistence and AMD machine-check helpers are no-effect entry points in this configuration, with the AMD memory-error predicate reporting negative and AMD feature init doing nothing.

Scalable MCA bank taxonomy enumerates many platform functional blocks such as coherent fabric, accelerators, decoder, execution, floating point, fetch, caches, load-store, memory controllers, interconnects, IO, security processors and management units, ending with a count sentinel for the number of bank kinds.

Memory-encryption lifecycle helpers are no-effect entry points in this configuration, covering subsystem init, early arch setup, early encrypt and decrypt, boot-data map and unmap, early init, kernel encryption, enablement, confidential-VC handling setup, and freeing of decrypted memory.

Memory-encryption mask and confidential status values are both defined as zero in this configuration, and the hypercall-based early encrypt-decrypt state change is a no-effect helper while early encrypted-state change reports success.

One configuration exposes the encryption mask through a shared variable while the fallback configuration always reports zero, and decrypted-data annotation either selects a dedicated decrypted section or expands to nothing.
Secure physical address derivation combines the normal physical translation with the memory-encryption mask using a bitwise inclusive-or, in both normal and nodebug forms.
Processor microcode identity uses a compact signature record plus a per-CPU record pairing that signature with an opaque blob pointer; signature carries stepping identity, feature flags and revision.
Microcode load helpers for primary and secondary CPUs and resume path are no-effect entry points, while the loader-disabled predicate reports that loading remains enabled.

Intel microcode update layout pairs a fixed header with trailing payload words; the header carries versioning, identity, integrity, loader and platform fields plus data, total and metadata sizes, minimum required version and reserved space.

Microcode sizing and typing facts are a default payload size of two thousand bytes, a header size derived from the header record, and distinct small integer type codes for microcode versus in-field scan content.

Microcode revision query clears the revision facility, performs a processor identification step, then reads back the current revision; datasize query falls back to the default payload size when the header leaves it unset.
Model-specific register read helper exposes a 64-bit facility value as two separate 32-bit halves, preserving a single underlying read.
NMI microcode-handler enablement is either governed by a dynamic branch control or unconditionally reports disabled, depending on configuration.
VM protection-bit derivation maps each of the four low-order key bits onto a distinct protection-key VM bit, combining the selected bits inclusively.
PCI configuration-space enablement probes for older AMD families and firmware tables are no-effect helpers in this configuration.

Address-space context flag indices assign successive small integers to 32-bit uprobe mode, vsyscall presence, linear-address-mask locking, forced tagged shared-virtual-addressing, and no-track selection.

Per-address-space x86 context holds a unique nonzero identifier, TLB generation counter, trim scheduling state, optional local-descriptor state and flags, optional masking state, a mutex, virtual dynamic linker base and image, performance-counter permission, optional protection-key allocation state, and optional broadcast-TLB global address-space state.
Initial address-space context starts with identifier one and an initialized context mutex.
Local descriptor table handle holds a pointer to descriptor entries, an entry count, and a mapping slot index where negative means no alias mapping is installed.

Local descriptor lifecycle either clears and initializes table state with a semaphore or compiles to successful no-effect helpers; runtime load clears the table and table switch asserts non-preemptible context without further action in the shown fragments.

Local descriptor updates are serialized by a per-address-space semaphore, general context mutation by a per-address-space mutex, protection-key allocation state by the address-space read-write lock, and global address-space identifier teardown by a raw spinlock with interrupts saved.

Linear-address masking state is snapshotted once per use to avoid races with concurrent enablement, duplicated as a pair on fork, reset to an all-ones untag mask, and DMA compatibility holds when masking is off or forced tagged addressing is selected; the fallback configuration reports no masking and empty duplication and reset.

Address-space context bringup initializes locking, assigns a fresh unique identifier, clears TLB generation, schedules trimming, establishes default protection-key and global-ID state, resets untag state, and initializes descriptor state; teardown releases descriptor and global-ID state.

Global address-space identifier moves from unassigned to assigned during use and back to unassigned on teardown, with freed values marked for reuse only after wrap-around flushing and availability accounting updated under lock.

Global identifier read returns zero when broadcast invalidation is unavailable or unassigned, otherwise returns an acquire-ordered value that must not lie in the dynamic range; the dynamic predicate tests membership below a fixed dynamic count and the fallback configuration always reports zero.

Address-space activation enters paravirtual state then performs an IRQ-off switch, duplication copies protection keys and masking state and enters paravirtual state before duplicating descriptors, exit notifies paravirtual and descriptor layers, and deactivation clears segment state with an additional shadow-stack release in one configuration.
Paravirtual address-space notifications either dispatch through the paravirtual operations table or compile to no-effect helpers when paravirtual support is absent.

Sixty-four-bit address-space detection depends on emulation configuration and a context flag, with one configuration unconditionally reporting false, while no-track status is a testable and settable context flag.

Access permission bypasses protection-key checks for instruction execution and for foreign mappings, otherwise defers to the rights register evaluation for the mapping key and write intent; mapping key is recovered from VM flag bits by masking and shifting.

Rights-register evaluation denies reads when the per-key access-disable bit is set and denies writes when either access-disable or write-disable is set; the register reads zero when OS key support is off, otherwise it comes from hardware with a cleared secondary input and discarded high half.
Module arch state optionally carries unwinder table metadata and always carries an indirect-trampoline page collection that is populated only when that mitigation is enabled.

Multiprocessor table limits appear in multiple configurations with bus maxima of thirty-two, two hundred sixty, and two hundred fifty-six, and interrupt-source maxima of two hundred fifty-six or four times the bus maximum.
Multiprocessor identification uses a four-character magic value and caps the configuration-table entry count at one thousand twenty-four.

In the shown configuration SMP discovery reports absent, table update is disabled, table discovery and parsing entry points alias to a generic no-operation, and reserved-table allocation is a no-effect helper.
Physical CPU presence handling either resets the map to contain only the supplied APIC identity or copies the current presence map to a caller buffer.

TLB handling requires table changes before generation increment before flush; global identifiers must not re-enter service before wrap flushing; linear masking reads must use one snapshot across CR3 and TLB state; kernel-thread switches can race masking enablement.

Descriptor tables need page-aligned restricted mappings to block privileged gates, and isolated page-table mode keeps user-invisible entries with dual alias slots so a new table can be installed without disturbing an older table still in use.
Context identifiers are never reused and zero is reserved as invalid.
